<entry id="U01370">
<head-word>שָׁלַף</head-word>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="U01229"> cmp. שָׁלֵו</xref>,
<xref rid="A00083"> a. שָׁלָה)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be lax, hang down, be loose, slip</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Denom. שָׁלִיף.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to loosen, take off, pull, draw a sword</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Lev. R. s. 34 יִשְׁלוֹף Ar. (ed. ישמוט) may he loosen (release), v. חָלַץ. Y. Kidd. I, 60
<sup>c</sup> top (ref. to Ruth IV, 7) מי ש' which took the shoe off (the buyer or the seller)? Num. R. s. 14
<sup>4</sup> מסמר … נוח לִשְׁלוֹף a nail with a big head is easily pulled; Pesik. R. s. 3. Midr. Till. to Ps. CXX אם יִשְׁלוֹף האדם וכ' if a man draws the sword which he has in his hand to slay his neighbor &c.; a. e.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִשְׁלַף</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be loosened, drawn</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 93; Yalk. ib. 150 ואינה נִשְׁלֶפֶת, v. תַּעַר.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִשְׁלִיף</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to pull, pluck the last growth</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 20; Yalk. ib. 32 על … שאדם מַשְׁלִיף שדהו אוכלה וכ' this (Gen. III, 18) was said with reference to these days, when one plucks his field over and again and eats it (the aftermath) &c., v. Pes. 118
<sup>a</sup></notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="U01371">
<head-word>שְׁלַף</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, 
<italic>to loosen, pull, draw</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Hos. IV, 11. Targ. Y. Num. XXXI, 8. Targ. Jud. III, 22. Targ. Y. Ex. III, 5; a. fr.—Targ. I Chr. I, 20 (play on שלף, ib.) ש' … לתחומיה (not לתחומיא) he drew the rivers into his domain.—Part. pass. שְׁלִיף. Targ. Y. I Deut. XXV, 10 (Y. II שְׁלוּפֵי Hebraism, 
<plural-form>pl., h. text חלוץ</plural-form>).—V. שְׁלִיף II.—Yeb. 102
<sup>b</sup> ממאי דהאי וחלצה … מִישְׁלַף הוא how do we know that this 
<italic>v’ḥal’tsah</italic> (Deut. XXV, 9) means taking off? Y. ib. XII, 13
<sup>a</sup> top ושַׁלְפַת סיניה and she took off his shoe. Sabb. 59
<sup>b</sup> דילמא שָׁלְפָא וכ' she might take off (her jewelry) and show it. Ib. מְשַׁלְּפָא (
<italic>Pa.</italic>). Ib. 82
<sup>a</sup> ולא שליף ירקא וכ' and that no vegetable will be pulled, and eaten by you, out of the bunch &c. Shebu. 31
<sup>a</sup> שְׁלוֹפוּ, v. פּוּזְמְקֵי. Erub. 11
<sup>b</sup> זיל שְׁלוֹף וכ' go and pull (the reeds) out, and throw them away; a. fr.—Trnsf. (cmp. נתר, שרי) 
<italic>to untie, annul</italic>. Gitt. 33
<sup>b</sup> מילתא … למִישְׁלְפָהּ an act performed in the presence of ten persons, requires ten for revoking it; a. e.—Yeb. 109
<sup>b</sup> ערבי שלציון דעבדי שְׁלוֹף דוץ the guarantors of Shaltsiyon, where they practice ‘pull and stick in’, release the debtor and seize the guarantor.—Sabb. 90
<sup>a</sup>, a. e. שלוף דוץ, v. שְׁלוֹף.—[Sabb. 98
<sup>b</sup>; Yalk. Ex. 370, v. שַׁלְחֵף.]</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>שַׁלֵּיף</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> same.</definition>
<notes> Targ. O. Lev. XIV, 40 (h. text חלץ). Ib. 43 (some ed. 
<italic>Pe.</italic>).—Yeb. 102
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to החלצו, Num. XXXI, 3) שַׁלּוּפֵי מביתא וכ' it means tearing away from home to war. M. Kat. 4
<sup>b</sup>, v. דָּלַל. Sabb. 59
<sup>b</sup>, v. supra; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Ithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִשְׁתַּלֵּיף, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Ithpe.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִשְׁתְּלִיף</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be drawn; to be loosened, to slip</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Ez. XXI, 15 (h. text הוחדה). Targ. II Kings VI, 5. Targ. Is. XXXIII, 20 (h. text יסע); a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="U01372">
<head-word>שֶׁלֶף</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (preced.) [
<italic>that which is pulled out,</italic>] 
<italic>stubble field</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. B. Mets. IX, 29 אינו … נירה למניחה לפניו ש' it is not the same when he surrenders the land tilled (cleared), as when he surrenders it with the stubbles.—
<plural-form>Pl. שְׁלָפִים</plural-form>. Cant. R. to VI, 12 מלקטת בש' picked up (ears) among the stubbles.—Trnsf. constr. שִׁלְפֵי, שִׁי' 
<italic>the end</italic> of a period. Yeb. 116
<sup>b</sup> ש' קציר חטים היו it was towards the end of the wheat harvest. Sabb. 60
<sup>a</sup> ש' הגזירה היו (Ar. השמד; Ms. M. שליפי, corr. acc.; Ms. O. שלהי, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) it was the end of the period of persecution; Cant. R. to II, 5 בש' השמד.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="U01380">
<head-word>שָׁלַק</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (Shaf. of חלק, as שנק of חנק) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> (cmp. Assyr. שלק, Del. Assyr. Handw. 666) 
<italic>to dissect</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Bekh. 45
<sup>a</sup> מעשה … שׁשָׁלְקוּ זונה וכ' it happened that the disciples of R. Yishm. dissected the body of a prostitute that had been condemned to death &c.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> [
<italic>to make smooth,</italic>] 
<italic>to boil thoroughly, boil to a pulp, seethe</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Maasr. IV, 1 הכובש חשׁוֹלֵק וכ' he who presses, boils, or salts (vegetables, olives &c.) … is bound to give tithes. Tosef. Bets. II, 15 ש' הימנו וכ' if he seethed a small portion of the Passover lamb, contrad. to בישל. Naz. VI, 9 (45
<sup>b</sup>) היה מבשל … או שׁוֹלְקָן Y. ed. a. Bab. (Mish. ed. שְׁלָקָן) having cooked or seethed the peace-offering; a. fr.—Part. pass. שָׁלוּק; f. שְלוּקָה. Y. ib. 55
<sup>c</sup> top מתני' אמרה הש' קרוי מבושל this Mishnah indicates that ‘seethed’ is called cooked. Ned. VI, 1 הנודר מן המבושל מותר בצלי ובש' he who vows abstinence from ‘what is cooked’ is permitted to eat what is roasted or seethed. Ukts. II, 6 ביצה ש' a hard-boiled egg; Tosef. ib. II, 15; ביצה ש' וביצה טרמיסא (read: טרומיטא) a hard-boiled egg, or an egg boiled down to a pill, v. טְרוֹמִיטָא; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>שִׁילֵּק</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to make smooth</italic>, (of melons) 
<italic>to trim and rub</italic>.</definition>

<sup>20</sup> לא יצאת אותה שנה ולא שינתה ולא שִׁילְּשָׁה וכ' not that year passed, nor the second, nor the third, when &c., i.e. within three years these things occurred; a. e.</notes></sense>

<notes> B. Bath. X, 7 יְשַׁלְּשׁוּ they should write the grandfather’s name in the document.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to divide into three parts</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ib. III, 4 מְשַׁלְּשִׁין ביניהם the fine is divided between them (the three sets of witnesses convicted of an alibi); Macc. I, 3. Ib. משלשין בממון ואין מש' במכות the monetary fine is divided, but not the punishment (but every one has to undergo the full punishment). Ab. Zar. 19
<sup>b</sup> לעולם יְשַׁלִּשׁ אדם שנותיו שליש וכ' a man should always divide his years (his time) into three parts, devoting one third to Bible, one to Mishnah &c.; Kidd. 30
<sup>a</sup> יַשְׁלִישׁ (
<italic>Hif.</italic>). Ex. R. s. 15
<sup>27</sup> הריני מְשַׁלְּשָׁם I will divide them among us three; a. fr.—
<italic>Part. pass.</italic> מְשׁוּלָּשׁ; f. מְשׁוּלֶּשֶׁת; 
<plural-form>pl. מְשׁוּלָּשִׁים, מְשׁוּלָּשִׁין; מְשׁוּלָּשׁוֹת</plural-form>
<italic>a</italic>) 
<italic>done for the third time</italic>. Ab. Zar. l. c., כתוב … ומש' בכתובים stated in the Torah, a second time in the Prophets, and a third time in Hagiographa; Meg. 31
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—
<italic>b</italic>) 
<italic>divided into three, arranged in three classes, threefold</italic>. Deut. R. s. 2
<sup>33</sup> (ref. to והשלשית, Zech. XIII, 8) אלו ישראל אנקראו שלישין שהם מש' וכ' that means Israel, who are called ‘thirds’, for they are divided into three classes, priests &c. Midr. Prov. to XXII, 20 (ref. to שלשים, ib.) כל מעשי תורה מש' היא מש' ואותיותיה מש' … שבט מש' וכ' all affairs of the Torah are threefold; itself is threefold: Torah, Prophets, and Hagiographa, and its signs are threefold: אמת (Truth); and it was given through a tribe third in order: Reuben, Shimeon, and Levi; משה מש' Moses the third born &c. Cant. R. to I, 1 
<pgbrk id="pg1589" />כל מעשיו … מש' היו all the events of that man’s (Solomon’s) life were marked by three stages (rise, fall, and rise).—B. Bath. X, 7 ואם היו מש' and if the names are alike up to the grandfather (v. supra); a. fr.—Y. Shebi. I, 33
<sup>b</sup>, v. מְשׁוּלָּשׁ.—
<italic>c</italic>) 
<italic>developed to one third of the full growth</italic>, v. מְשׁוּלָּשׁ.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition> (apocop. of שִׁלְשֵׁל)

<xref rid="U01398">שִׁלְשֵׁל I</xref>.</definition>

<senses>

<sup>a</sup>) מעשה שׁשִׁלְשְׁלוּהוּ לים וכ' it happened at ʿAsia with one whom they let down into the sea (as diver), and (in hauling him up) they brought up nothing but his leg.; Y. ib. 15

<italic>mark, name, title, nature, denomination</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pes. III, 3 לא תקרא לה שם וכ' she must not name it (declare it to be Ḥallah) until it is baked. Ter. III, 5 האומר … קרא שם if one says, the priest’s portion of this pile is in it …, he has named it (designated it as T’rumah). Gen. R. s. 25 (ref. to Gen. V, 29) לא השם הוא המדרש … הוא השם וכ' the name (נח) and the interpretation (ינחמנו) do not correspond; it ought to be either &c. Ber. II, 8 ליטול … השם, v. נָטַל. Macc. I, 2 לא השם המביאו וכ' the title (the legal text) under which the false witness is doomed to lashes, is not the one under which he is bound to pay indemnity. Kinn. I, 3 משם אחד sacrificial birds of the same denomination (intended for the same class of cases), opp. משני שמות of different denominations. Sabb. XII, 3 משם אחד two letters of the alphabet of the same name (אא, בב &c.), opp. משתי שמות two different letters (אב &c.). Ib. שם קטן משם גדול וכ' a small name or word as a part (or abbreviation) of a larger one, as שם as a part of שמעון, of שמואל &c. Ib. 103
<sup>b</sup> שתי אותיות והן שם אחד two identical letters which represent a word, (as שש, which may stand for שֵׁשׁ or שָׂשׂ) &c. Shebu. 3
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. לא מן השם הוא זה וכ' this comes not under this title (this is not the real reason), but it is because &c. Ker. III, 4 אינו מן השם the offence is not of the same class. Macc. 4
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. (על חבירו) מוציא שם רע who spreads an evil report about his neighbor (injures his reputation). Ber. 17
<sup>a</sup> גדל בשם טוב וכ' who has grown up with a good name, and departed life with a good name; a. v. fr.—Esp. הַשֵּׁם or שֵׁם 
<italic>the Divine Name, the Tetragrammaton</italic>, contradist. to כינוי attribute; in gen. 
<italic>the Lord</italic>. Snh. VII, 5 המגדף … שיפרש השם the blasphemer is not punishable, unless he uses the Name explicitly. Ib. 8 המקלל … בַּשֵּׁם he that curses his father or his mother is not punishable, unless he curses them with the Name. Ib. 56
<sup>a</sup> בידך את השם בכינוי (not בכינויים) if he curses God by using a divine attribute. Ib. עד שיברך שם בשם unless he curses God and pronounces the Name. Yoma III, 8; IV, 2; VI, 2 (בשם) אנא השם I pray, O Lord (pronouncing the Tetragrammaton). Ib. כשהיו שומעים שם המפורש שהוא יוצא וכ' when they heard the Tetragrammaton pronounced &c., v. פָּרַשׁ. Ib. IV, 1 אחד … לַשֵּׁם on one of the lots was written ‘unto the Lord’; של שם the lot bearing the inscription ‘unto the Lord’; a. v. fr.; v. שָׁמַיִם.—Especial uses: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁ־ 
<italic>the same as, as well as</italic>. Ber. IX, 5 חייב אדם … כשם שמברך וכ' a man is bound to bless God for what is evil as well as he blesses for what is good. Ib. 62
<sup>a</sup> כשם שנפרעין וכ' as well as the dead are called to account &c., v. סַפְדָּן. Sot. V, 1 כשם שהמים … כך וכ' as the waters test her, so do they test him. Ib. כשם שאסורה וכ', v. בָּעַל; a. v. fr.—בְּשֵׁם, מִשֵּׁם 
<italic>in the name of, in behalf of</italic>. Meg. 15
<sup>a</sup> כל האומר דכר בשם אומרו וכ' he who relates a thing in the name of him who said it (gives credit to authority), brings redemption into the world. Peah II, 4 מִשְּׁמוֹ in his own name (as his individual opinion). Y. Taan. I, 64
<sup>a</sup> הלכה … שאמר משם וכ' the rule follows the opinion of …, who said in behalf of &c.; a. v. fr.—לְשֵׁם 
<italic>for the purpose of, for the sake of, as; with reference to</italic>. Gitt. 24
<sup>b</sup> כתב רחמנא לה לִשְׁמָהּ the text (Deut. XXIV, 3) says, ‘unto her’, that means, that it must be written especially for her. Yeb. 47
<sup>b</sup>, v. שׁוּם II.—Snh. 99
<sup>b</sup> העוסק בתורה לשמה who studies the Law for its own sake (for no selfish ends). Pes. 50
<sup>b</sup> לעולם יעסוק … אע"פ שלא לשמה … בא לשמה by all means let a man engage in the study of the Law and in good deeds, even 
<pgbrk id="pg1591" />if not for their own sake, for through the work for a selfish purpose he will arrive at the stage of doing good for its own sake. Ib. 13
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. שחטן לִשְׁמָן וכ' if he slaughtered them as such (as festive sacrifices) &c.; זרק דמן שלא לשמן if he sprinkled their blood, having in mind another purpose (another class of sacrifices). Gen. R. s. 25 לשם קרבנו נקרא he was named (נח) with reference to his sacrifice (ניחח, Gen. VIII, 2</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>; לשם נחת וכ' he was named (נח) with reference to the rest of the ark (ותנח, Gen. VIII, 4); Yalk. ib.</definition>
<notes> 42 על שם וכ'; a. v. fr.—עַל שֵׁם (abbrev. ע"ש) 
<italic>with reference to, because</italic>. Y. Taan. II, beg. 65
<sup>a</sup> על שם ואנכי וכ' as a reference to (what Abraham said,) ‘and I am but dust and ashes’ (Gen. XVIII, 27). Gen. R. s. 23, v. טְבַרְיָא; a. fr.; v. שׁוּם II.—
<plural-form>Pl. שֵׁמוֹת,</plural-form> constr. שְׁמוֹת. Kinn. l. c. Gen. R. s. 26 כל הש' הללו וכ' all these names indicate rebellion &c., v. מַרְדּוּת I. B. Mets. 114
<sup>b</sup> עובר בכל הש' הללו is guilty under all these titles (texts). Shebu. 35
<sup>a</sup> יש ש' שנמחקין ויש ש' וכ' there are divine names which may be erased, and such as may not be erased. Y. R. Hash. I, 56
<sup>d</sup> bot. שְׁ' המלאכים, v. מַלְאָךְ; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>שִׂימֵּחַ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to make glad, cheer</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Bath. 10
<sup>b</sup> יְשַׂמֵּחַ את אשתו בדבר מצוה Ms. M. (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.) let him make his wife cheerful by means of a good deed. R. Hash. 6

<sup>b</sup>. Pes. 109
<sup>a</sup> חייב אדם לְשַׂמֵּחַ וכ' man is bound to gladden his children and the members of his household on the festival; במה מְשַׂמְּחָם wherewith should he gladden them? Keth. 8
<sup>a</sup> (in marriage benedictions) מְשַׂמֵּחַ ציון בבניה who gladdens Zion through (restoring to her) her children; משמח חתן וכלה who gladdens bridegroom and bride; מש' חתן עם הכלה who gladdens the bridegroom with the bride; שַׂמֵּח תְּשַׂמַּח … כשַׂמֵּחֲךָ וכ' mayest thou gladden the beloved friends, as thou didst gladden thy creature (Adam) &c.; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="U01450">
<head-word>שָׂמֵחַ</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> preced.) 
<italic>bright, joyful, joyous</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Kidd. 66
<sup>a</sup> היה ש' שמחה וכ' he rejoiced greatly (prepared a great festival), and invited &c. Ber. 5
<sup>a</sup>, v. עָצֵב. Ib. 9
<sup>b</sup> אדם … וש' במצות he is a great man and glad when he can do good. Meg. 10
<sup>b</sup> אין הקב"ה ש' וכ' the Lord does not rejoice over the downfall of the wicked; a. v. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. שְׂמֵחִים, שְׂמֵחִין, שְׂמֵי'</plural-form>. Sabb. 145
<sup>b</sup>, v. מוֹעֵד. Yoma 21
<sup>b</sup> עניים ש' … עצבין the poor are glad (because provisions will be cheap), and the property owners are sorry; B. Bath. 147
<sup>a</sup>. Cant. R. to I, 10; Y. Ḥag. II, 77
<sup>b</sup> bot. והיו הדברים ש' וכ' and the words (of the Law which they quoted at the festive board) were as bright as when they were delivered from Sinai; a. fr.—
<italic>Fem</italic>. שְׂמֵחָה, שְׂמֵי'. Pesik. R. s. 20 כשנתן … ארץ ש' ושמים בוכין when the Lord gave Israel the Law, the earth was glad, and the heavens wept; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. שְׂמֵחוֹת, שְׂמֵי'</plural-form>. Ib. s. 21 בפנים ש' with a cheerful contenance; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="U01451">
<head-word>שִׂמְחָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> preced.) 
<italic>joy, rejoicing, festive occasion</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Keth. 8
<sup>a</sup> (in Chald. dict.) אפושי ש' בעלמא הוא it is merely an extension of the wedding joy (not a new festive occasion). Ib. מברך שהש' במעונו he says the benediction containing the words, ‘in whose dwelling there is joy.’ Y. B. Bath. IX, 16
<sup>d</sup> bot. שִׂמְחַת זכר the joy over the birth of a male child. Gen. R. s. 70; M. Kat. 8
<sup>b</sup> ש' בש', v. עָרב I; a. fr.—Esp. שמחת יום טוב, or ש' 
<italic>the rejoicing on the festival</italic> (Deut. XVI, 11; 14). R. Hash. 6
<sup>b</sup> איתה בש' she (woman) is included in the commandment to 
<pgbrk id="pg1594" />observe the festival with joy. Ḥag. 6
<sup>a</sup> חנה … מיחייבא בש' was not Hannah herself bound to visit the Temple in order to rejoice? Pes. 109
<sup>a</sup> בזמן … אין ש' אלא בבשר … אין ש' אלא ביין as long as the Temple stood, the festive rejoicing consisted in eating meat (of the peace-offering), … but now … the festive celebration consists in partaking of wine; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. שְׂמָחוֹת</plural-form>. Zeb. 102
<sup>a</sup> חמש ש' היתה וכ' Elisheba had five joys (distinctions) more than ordinary daughters of Israel: her brother-in-law (Moses) was king &c.; a. e.—ש' (מסכת) 
<italic>S’maḥoth</italic>, one of the small treatises of Talmud Babli, euphem. for אבל רבתי, v. אֵבֶל.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="U01453">
<head-word>שָׁמַט</head-word>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> cmp. מוּט)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to slip</italic>; (act. verb) 
<italic>to loosen, detach; to carry off, steal</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Num. R. s. 4
<sup>20</sup> (ref. to II Sam. VI, 6) למה שָׁמְטוּ why did they slip (turn off)? M. Kat. 24
<sup>a</sup> שמטו חזירים וכ' swine dragged his body off. Y. Ber. III, 5
<sup>d</sup> bot., a. e. שׁוֹמֵט וכ', v. קְלִבִּנְטִירִין. Ib. מטה … שׁוֹמְטָן ודיו in the case of a bed the poles of which are movable, one (in mourning) detaches them, and that is sufficient; Y. Ned. VII, end, 40
<sup>c</sup> שומטו (corr. acc.). B. Mets. 104
<sup>a</sup> שׁוֹמְטוֹ מעל גבי בניו he may take it (the pledge) from the back of his (the debtor’s) sons. Ex. R. s. 43 והם שׁוֹמְטִים וכ', v. טֶטְרָאמוּלִי. Y. Keth. V, 30
<sup>b</sup> היתה שׁוֹמֶטֶת עצמה וכ' she slipped away from under him; Sot. 9
<sup>b</sup> נִשְׁמְטָה (
<italic>Nif.</italic>). Gen. R. s. 14 שׁוֹמְטָהּ, v. צָרַר I. Pesik. R. s. 20 נִשְׁמוֹט אותה let us abandon her (that she may not find her way home); מיד שְׁמָטוּהָ (not שמוטה) and so they abandoned her. Lev. R. s. 34 יִשְׁמוֹט, v. חָלַץ. Gen. R. s. 20 שומט גידין וכ' it (the serpent) draws out fibres (v. גִּיד) and eats them. Midr. Till. to Ps. CXIV (ref. to Deut. IV, 34 גוי מקרב גוי) כאדם ששומט את העובר וכ' as a man draws an embryo out of its mother’s womb. Ib. למדנו צער לנִשְׁמָט לשומט מנין we learn here that there was pain for the body drawn out (Israel), whence do we learn that it was painful for him that drew out (for the Lord who redeemed them)?; a. fr.—Part. pass. שָׁמוּט; f. שְׁמוּטָה. Ḥull. 54
<sup>a</sup> ש' ושחוטה וכ' if the trachea was found detached, yet cut through, the animal is 
<italic>kasher</italic>; שא"א לש' וכ' for it is impossible that a loose trachea should be cut through (therefore the detachment must have taken place after the ritual cutting). Ib. 57
<sup>a</sup>, a. e. שְׁמוּטַת ורך an animal with a dislocated thigh-bone; שמוטת וד with a dislocated foreleg; a. e.—V. שָׁמוּט.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִשְׁמַט</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be detached, slip away</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Midr. Till. l. c., v. supra. Sot. l. c., v. supra. Num. R. s. 1
<sup>8</sup> הר חורב שעליו נִשִׁמְטָה החרב וכ' it is named mount Horeb, because on it the sword (of judgment) was unsheathed (for crimes); (Yalk. ib. 684 נמשכה; Yalk. Ps. 796 נמתחה). Macc. II, 1, v. קַתְּ. Sifra Emor, ch. II, Par. 3 (expl. שרוע, Lev. XXI, 18) שנשמטה יריכו (Rabad שנשתרבבה) whose hip is dislocated. Cant. R. to V, 16 (ממנו) נשמטה נפשו his soul slipped away (from him), he fainted; a. fr.—[Tosef. ‘Uktsin I, 2 (Tbul Yom III) נשמטין, read with ed. Zuck. נִכְסָסִין.]</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>שִׁמֵּט</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to loosen, pluck</italic>, esp. 
<italic>to thin</italic> a thicket of reeds.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Shebi. I, 7; Y. ib. II, 33
<sup>d</sup> top מְשַׁמְּטִין בקנים you may thin reeds (in the Sabbatical year); מקום … ולְשַׁמֵּט וכ' where it is customary to clear vines and to thin reeds before &c.; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to drag forth</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pesik. R. s. 17 ומְשַׁמְּטִים הבכורות מבין וכ' and the dogs dragged the dead bodies of the first-born out of the burial caves; Yalk. Ex. 186; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition> (v. 
<xref rid="U01456">שְׁמִטָּה</xref>) 
<italic>to cause release from debt; to cause cessation of field labor</italic>; (neut. verb) 
<italic>to come under the law of limitation of the Sabbatical year</italic>; (of the ground) 
<italic>to rest</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Shebi. X, 1 שביעית מְשַׁמֶּטֶת את המלוה וכ' the Sabbatical year causes cancellation of (cash) debts, whether verbal or written; הקפת … אינה משמטת, v. הַקָּפָה; שכר שכיר אינו מְשַׁמֵּט a hired man’s wages do not come under the law of 
<italic>sh’miṭṭah</italic>; ib. 2 המוסר … אינן משמטין (not אינו) if one hands his notes over to the court, they are not subject to the law of limitation; ib. האונס … וכל מעשה ב"ד אינן משמטין fines for outrage …, and all obligations arising from legal procedures do not come under the law &c.; ib. 3, v. פְּרוֹזְבּוֹל; [Y. ed. מַשְׁמִיט, מַשְׁמִיטִין &c. 
<italic>Hif.</italic> interch. with 
<italic>Pi</italic>.]. Sifra B’ḥuck., Par. 2, ch. VII אני אמרתי … ומשמטים לי אחת וכ' I have told you that you may sow six years, and let the ground rest for me one year, that you may know &c.; עמדו וגלו והיא תְשַׁמֵּט מאליה כל שמיטים וכ' go ye and be carried into exile, and it (the land) will rest of itself (making up for) all the Sabbatical years &c.; Yalk. Lev. 675 והיא תַשְׁמִיט מאיליה עד שתרצה לפני כל שמיטין וכ'. Ab. d’R. N. ch. XXXVIII הואיל ואין אתם משמיטין אותה היא תְשַׁמֵּט אתכם (ed. Schechter ואי אתם משמטים את הארץ) because you do not let the earth rest, she will abandon you; ומספר ירחים שאי אתם משמיטין אותה היא תשמט מאליה (ed. Schechter שאין אתם משמטים) and according to the number of months that you fail to let her rest, she will rest of herself. Gitt. 36
<sup>a</sup> בזמן שאתה משמט … משמט כספים when thou art bound to let the ground rest, thou art bound to cancel debts; a. fr.—Snh. 97
<sup>a</sup> כשם שהשביעית משמטת … כך העולם משמט וכ' as the Sabbatical year causes cessation of field work once every seven years, so shall the world rest (be waste) one millennium in every seven millenniums.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to remit a debt</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gitt. 37
<sup>b</sup> המחזיר חוב … יאמר לו משמט אני וכ' if a person pays a debt in the Sabbatical year, he (the creditor) must say, ‘I remit’ (and have no claim): but if he (the debtor) says, ‘nevertheless’, he may accept; Sabb. 148
<sup>b</sup>; Sifré Deut. 112; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—5)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to abandon, send away</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ab. d’R. N. l. c., v. supra.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>

<sup>b</sup> אם יִשְׁמַע וכ' if a man hears an improper word &c., v. שָׁפָה II. Ber. 13
<sup>a</sup> the text (Deut. VI, 4) says ‘hear’ (or ‘understand’), בכל לשון שאתה שׁוֹמֵעַ recite the Sh’mʿa in whatever language you understand. R. Hash. III, 7 אם קול שופר ש' if he heard the sound of a Shofar; ואם קול הברה ש', v. הֲבָרָה. Y. Hor. I, 46

<sense>

<notes> Ber. 6
<sup>a</sup> אין תפלה … נִשְׁמַעַת וכ' man’s prayer is heard only in the house of prayer. Y. ib. V, end, 9
<sup>b</sup> שׁנִשְׁמְעָה תפלתו that his prayer will be heard (his petition be granted). Erub. 18
<sup>b</sup> כל בית שׁנִשְׁמָעִין וכ' a house in which the words of the Law are heard by night will never be destroyed. Yeb. 65
<sup>b</sup> כשם … דבר הנִשְׁמָע וכ' as well as it is proper to say a thing that has been heard (to mention one’s authority), so it is proper not to say a thing that has not been heard (for which you cannot cite your authority); a. fr.</notes></sense>

<sup>a</sup> הִשָּׁמְעִי לי (ed.

<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. לא ש' לי הא שמעתתא this tradition is not known to me. Pes. 34

<italic>and</italic> those’: it stands proved. Y. M. Kat. III, 83

<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
